subject: Model shortlist, context depth and capacity assumptions for Cardinal Data onboarding
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@cardinaldata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Model shortlist, context depth and capacity assumptions for Cardinal Data onboarding

Elena —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Per our discussion, attached is the traffic snapshot you shared (CD-traffic-snapshot.csv) and my preliminary take on model choices and sizing assumptions. High-level asks from us before the implementation kickoff:

- Confirm the expected steady-state QPS and the 99th percentile burst window (you indicated ~120 QPS steady / 450 QPS burst for a 10min window).
- Confirm whether long-form retrieval responses (document synthesis) require a single 32k context or if a segmented multi-request approach is acceptable.
- Any hard latency SLO (p90/p95) for real-time chat flows? We assumed p95 < 700ms.

Current shortlist and reasoning (subject to your confirmation):
1) Open-32k-v2 (32k context) — preferred for single-call document synthesis; higher cost but simpler integration.
2) Opti-8k-q4 (8k quantized) — good for chat + retrieval when we can prefetch context and use prefix/KV cache. Lower token cost.
3) Fast-1.5 (lower-capacity, cheaper) — fallback for non-critical flows and ingestion pipelines.

Sizing notes (back-of-envelope):
- Avg token length per chat interaction: 420 tokens (user + assistant).
- Estimated daily active sessions: 28k — yields ~11.8M tokens/day in steady mix (exact numbers in follow-up table).
- Peak hour multiplier: 2.3x.

Next steps I propose: Monica to finalize token burn spreadsheet with per-flow breakdown, Ben to run a quick throughput simulation against Opti-8k-q4 and Open-32k-v2 on our dev pool, and us to align on a canary schedule (2 weeks after kickoff).

If those owners are good, I can book a 30-min ops sync tomorrow to lock ranges.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Attachments: CD-traffic-snapshot.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Elena Morales <elena@cardinaldata.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 12:15:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Model shortlist, context depth and capacity assumptions for Cardinal Data onboarding

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick clarifications from our side:

- QPS: steady ~110–130 QPS, bursts up to ~520 QPS but those bursts are <6 minutes typically.
- Long-form synthesis: we prefer single-call 32k for the summarization use case (less complexity on our side), but can accept a segmented approach if the cost delta is material.
- Latency: product team wants p95 < 800ms for chat; for synthesis it's OK to be higher (p95 < 2s).

On cost: can you give us a delta estimate between using Open-32k-v2 for synthesis vs doing a segmented 8k flow plus assembly? If the difference is >25% we'd likely push for segmented.

Also: procurement will need a short MOP (mutual action plan) and a technical evidence pack (SOC2 pointers + KV cache notes). We've looped procurement, they may send a checklist next.

Elena
Head of Product
Cardinal Data

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@cardinaldata.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:37:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Model shortlist, context depth and capacity assumptions for Cardinal Data onboarding

Elena / Jonas —

I ran an initial token-estimate sheet (attached: cardinal-token-estimates.xlsx) and a quick cost delta for the two synthesis approaches. Key takeaways:

- Using Open-32k-v2 for single-call synthesis (median doc size 18k tokens) increases per-synthesis token cost by ~48% vs segmented 8k calls + server-side assembly, assuming a 10% duplicate prompt overhead for segmented calls. If Cardinal is sensitive to unit cost, segmented is materially cheaper.

- For chat flows, Opti-8k-q4 gives ~2.1x cost savings vs Open-8k (non-quantized) while keeping p95 latency within the 650–750ms range on our Dedicated dev pool with batching enabled.

- Caching strategy: we recommend prefix/KV caching for recurrent retrieval hits. With a 30% hit rate (conservative), expected token burn drops ~22% for conversational flows. We'll provide a small SDK snippet to enable warmed cache on session start.

- Throughput assumptions for canary (10% traffic): plan for 12k real-time sessions/day -> ~1.3M tokens/day on canary. Benchmarks attached. Ben: if you can run the Opti-8k-q4 sim and drop the p95 numbers into the sheet, we can finalize the canary window.

Action items:
- Monica: finalize and lock token-estimates.xlsx (I’ll update with Ben's sim results).
- Ben: throughput sim on Opti-8k-q4 + Open-32k-v2 by EOD today.
- Elena: confirm whether procurement wants single-call 32k hard requirement or whether segmented is acceptable (this will change scope).

I'll add SOC2 pointers and KV cache notes to the Notion checklist (link below).

Thanks,
Monica
Solutions Engineer, Implementation
Redwood Inference

Attachments: cardinal-token-estimates.xlsx (Excel, 96KB)
Related: https://notion.so/redwood/cardinal-onboarding-checklist-9f3a

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@cardinaldata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, procurement@cardinaldata.com
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:02:57 -0700
Subject: Re: Model shortlist, context depth and capacity assumptions for Cardinal Data onboarding

Elena —

Appreciate the quick answers. Plan below and proposed schedule:

1) Canary approach (10% traffic) starting Mon, Nov 1 — run 2 weeks. Goal: validate p95 latency and token burn with Opti-8k-q4 + segmented synthesis flow. If perf looks good and cost is >25% better, we will default to segmented. Otherwise, switch to Open-32k-v2 for synthesis (targeted rollout).

2) Owners: Monica (token estimates & SOC2/technical evidence pack), Ben (throughput sims + dev-pool tests), Jonas (canary plan + rollout gating).

3) Deliverables before kickoff (Oct 28):
- Final token-estimates.xlsx (Monica)
- Opti-8k-q4 sim results with p50/p95/p99 latency (Ben)
- Procurement MOP doc template and evidence pointers (I’ll draft; procurement@cardinaldata.com please confirm required fields)

I scheduled a 30-min ops sync for Fri Oct 23 11:00–11:30 PT to finalize numbers (invitation sent). Please accept if that works.

If procurement needs a DocuSign statement covering data residency & retention, I can attach a standard DS to the MOP.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this down.
Jonas
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
